notes: The Ryukyu Islands: Amami Oshima, Okinawa (Yanbaru), Miyako, Ishigaki, Iriomote and Yonaguni. All the island endemics (Okinawa Rail, Okinawa Woodpecker, Amami Woodcock, Lidth's Jay, Amami Thrush, Ryukyu and Okinawa Robins, Iriomote Tit, Ryukyu Minivet, Japanese Woodpigeon), the southern birds that barely reach Japan (Whistling Green-Pigeon, Crested Serpent-Eagle, Ruddy Kingfisher, White-shouldered Starling, Malayan Night Heron, Black-backed Swamphen, Light-vented Bulbul), the herons, crakes and terns of the rice fields and reefs, and the migrants that stop on the islands. Okinawa, Amami and Yaeyama are one pack because the GeoModel cannot tell them apart and a birder usually combines them. The model has no view on the endemics, so the list is hand-picked from eBird's lists for Okinawa and Amami. Black-backed Swamphen (purswa4) is not in the country species table for Japan and was left out. Photos are review-agent picks from unreviewed candidates (not approved on production): check them on /trip-photos. Shaky picks: Cinnamon Bittern (many candidates are other bitterns; selected are female/juvenile-type small bitterns, ID low confidence); Ruddy Kingfisher (rejected purple-backed dwarf-kingfisher-like birds); Light-vented Bulbul (mostly distant photos); Malayan Night Heron (many juveniles); Black Paradise-Flycatcher (chestnut-backed males skipped for ID doubt); Japanese Woodpigeon (few clear photos; 177607 pale-headed bird moderate confidence); Whistling Green-Pigeon (some doubt vs White-bellied Green-Pigeon); Amami Woodcock (nocturnal flash shots); Grey-faced Buzzard (mostly flight shots); Iriomote Tit (only 2 usable; others blurry/dark or doubtful); Watercock (non-breeding/female ID less sure); Black-naped Tern (small/distant); Ryukyu Minivet (lookalike Ashy Minivet; ID by locale); Pacific Swallow (Barn Swallow lookalike doubt); Ryukyu Flycatcher (lookalike Narcissus Flycatcher).
